messages:
alex (Sales): Hey @maya — heads-up, Acme POC is blocked on SSO + SCIM. Hosted API keys work for test calls, but they can't authenticate into the Dedicated/PVC control plane. IdP assertion is being rejected (Invalid NameID format) and SCIM provisioning calls return 400 'missing userName'. Jordan from Acme is on the thread.

jordan (Acme IT): sharing a couple of logs we see on our side:
```
SAML error: AssertionConsumerService rejected - NameIDFormat="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient"
SAML verification: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
SCIM POST /Users -> 400 {"detail":"missing userName"}
```

maya (SE): thanks. Two likely root causes:
- NameID format mismatch — Private/Dedicated setups default to emailAddress for secure account mapping.
- SCIM mapping missing required fields (userName or externalId).
Can you paste the IdP metadata XML or metadata URL and one example SCIM POST (headers + body)? Also FYI Dedicated control plane requires management API IP allowlist for SCIM provisioning calls.

jordan (Acme IT): metadata URL is https://idp.acme.com/metadata.xml. We do rotate certs weekly — could that explain the signature errors?

maya (SE): Yes, rotating certs without auto-refresh breaks signature verification. Options:
1) Short-term: upload the current cert into the Redwood Console SSO settings.
2) Long-term: provide the metadata URL and we'll enable IdP metadata auto-refresh on your Private deployment so we pull new certs automatically.

For Okta-style settings please use:
```
NameID policy: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress
Attribute statements:
  email -> user.email
  givenName -> user.firstName
  familyName -> user.lastName
```
And an example SCIM user mapping payload we expect (example):
```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "{{user.email}}",
  "name": {"givenName": "{{user.firstName}}", "familyName": "{{user.lastName}}"},
  "externalId": "{{user.id}}"
}
```

nate (Security): please also provide a sample SAML response header (so we can check the signature algorithm) and the X.509 cert thumbprint. For Private deployments the SCIM bearer token must be treated as a secret and rotated/stored in your KMS; we will not accept a long-lived plaintext token. If you want automated metadata refresh we require the metadata URL be HTTPS with a valid CA or signed metadata distribution.

jordan (Acme IT): we can provide the SAML response and thumbprint. Uploading cert into the console is doable short-term. Quick Q: for Dedicated pool access — we assumed an API key would be enough for provisioning?

maya (SE): Hosted API keys are fine for hosted endpoints. For Dedicated/Private POCs we need the SSO config + SCIM provisioning set up and the provisioning IPs allowlisted on the control plane so the IdP can call the SCIM endpoints. I'll open an Ops request to add Acme's provisioning IPs and attach a short runbook for the IdP steps.

alex (Sales): I'll schedule a 30-min troubleshooting call tomorrow 10:00am PT with Jordan + Maya + Nate to walk through cert upload and SCIM mapping. Thanks all :thumbsup:
